Disability is really something shaped unfortunately by what is mostly unknown, taboo and fear mongering. If you’re prepared to be a parent you should accept a child in any way they’re born given it’s not something that would make the child suffer (but even then with adequate medicine that can be supported). Disability, illness and disease are all parts of humanity and as parents that can also still equate with quality of life! There is no such thing as a “perfect” child and if that’s what a couple want then maybe they should re evaluate their decision. I’m also of the opinion women should be able to make decisions regarding their bodies and abortion but it sounds more of an uneducated decision rather than one of thought, care and compassion. There is beauty, love and life with disabilities…it’s not always the first picture you think, nor is it simple or easy but is so rich and fulfilling x

While you can’t plan for everything, or every challenge, we can plan and control what we can control. You want to give the good stories? So what happens when they end up in the worst case? I think it’s more then diversity? What about the life long medical cost? Which is absolutely astronomical in a country that does not have free healthcare? Nobody is paying those cost but them. Not to mention the commitment of parenting a disabled child is different than a non disabled child, let’s be intellectually honest on the commitment level. My child that is not disabled will leave and live independently and work and be independent from me by the early their early to mid 20s. Your adult disabled child will probably need a caretaker even after you die. Who’s doing that? How are you paying for it? Again, let’s have hard conversations… that are fully intellectually honest and not just brush it with a brush and call it accepting diversity. It is a much larger responsibility and conversation than that. And telling parents they should just not live in fear is absurd. It’s not fear, it’s living in the medical realities of it.
